text.p: French airline, L'Aeropostale has taken delivery of its fifteenth Boeing 737-300 quick change aircraft.
"The aircraft, which was used by L'Aeropostale in 1996 to transport freight has been modified to "quick change" configuration by U.S. company, Pemco," L'Aeropostale said.
It was the first time a 737-300F had been transformed into "quick change" configuration, the airline added.
The new 737-300 QC aircraft is leased from Swedish company, Indigo Aircraft, for a five-year period.
L'Aeropostale's fleet comprises 21 aircraft: 15 737-300QCs, two 737-200QCs, two 737-200Fs and two 727-200Fs.
It carries freight by night between France's major cities for the French post office and its express arm, Chronopost, TAT Express and Air France Europe.

By day, L'Aeropostale's fleet is used to transport passengers on behalf of the Air France group and Air Charter, on scheduled and charter services. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
